title: Export offline benchmark summary in perf-canary slice format
author: Noah Patel
description: Context: As we roll out the production perf-regression canary, we keep running into "is this real or just baseline drift / slice mismatch?" questions when a canary slice (model + gpu_sku + runtime_build + scheduler_mode + prompt shape) looks worse. Benchmark-lab already produces detailed offline results, but the output format is not directly comparable to the canary metric slices and requires ad-hoc spreadsheets to line up fields. This PR adds a new exporter that emits a compact benchmark summary in the same slice dimensions (and naming) used by perf-canary dashboards/alerts, so we can do sanity checks and drift investigations quickly. What this adds: (1) New CLI: `benchmark-lab export perf-canary-summary` that reads a benchmark run directory (or run id) and emits newline-delimited JSON (jsonl) or CSV. (2) Stable schema that mirrors prod canary slice keys: `model`, `model_revision` (if present), `quantization_profile` (optional), `gpu_sku`, `region` ("offline" by default unless provided), `runtime_build`, `runtime_git_sha` (if present), `scheduler_mode`, `kernel_family` (best effort), `prompt_shape_id`, `prefill_tokens`, `decode_tokens`, `streaming` (true/false), `batch_size`, `concurrency`, plus computed metrics: `latency_ms_p50`, `latency_ms_p95`, `ttft_ms_p50`, `ttft_ms_p95`, `tokens_per_second_mean`, `tokens_per_second_p50`, `tokens_per_second_p95`, and `sample_count`. (3) A "mapping" layer from existing benchmark-lab fields to perf-canary naming (e.g., `tok_s` -> `tokens_per_second_*`, `first_token_ms` -> `ttft_ms_*`). (4) Unit tests that assert field names/types and guard against accidental label churn, plus a golden snapshot for a representative run. (5) Documentation and an example invocation that produces files that can be ingested into the perf-canary backtesting notebook / quick diff script. Notes / decisions: - We keep `region` in the schema even for offline results because canary slices include it, and it makes it easier to join later; default is `offline` unless overridden. - `kernel_family` is best-effort: we populate if the run metadata includes kernel selection dumps; otherwise it is omitted (empty string in CSV). - Output is deterministic (sorted by model, gpu_sku, prompt_shape_id, streaming, batch_size, concurrency) to make diffs reviewable in PRs / incidents. - This does not change the benchmark runner itself; it is purely an export/transform step. Example output (jsonl, one record): {"model":"llama-3.1-70b-instruct","model_revision":"2026-01-28","quantization_profile":"fp16","gpu_sku":"H100-SXM","region":"offline","runtime_build":"runtime-1.27.0-rc3","runtime_git_sha":"8b1f3c2","scheduler_mode":"pinned_v2","kernel_family":"flashattn_v3","prompt_shape_id":"chat-short","prefill_tokens":512,"decode_tokens":256,"streaming":"false","batch_size":4,"concurrency":8,"latency_ms_p50":182.4,"latency_ms_p95":214.9,"ttft_ms_p50":37.1,"ttft_ms_p95":45.8,"tokens_per_second_mean":1842.7,"tokens_per_second_p50":1830.2,"tokens_per_second_p95":1764.8,"sample_count":120} Rollout plan: perf-canary team will use this exporter in ENG-2855 backtesting and during oncall regression triage to compare "prod canary slice" vs "offline expected slice" without manually re-labeling. Checklist: - [x] Added exporter CLI + docs - [x] Added schema tests + golden file - [x] Verified join keys match canary metric labels (`gpu_sku`, `scheduler_mode`, `runtime_build`) - [x] Ran exporter on 3 recent benchmark runs and spot-checked against raw stats
commits: schema: introduce stable PerfCanarySliceSummary fields + mapping helpers
tests: add golden snapshot + schema regression tests
docs: document exporter usage and downstream join keys
refactor: consolidate percentile computation for latency/ttft/tokens_per_second
review_conversation: Nadia Rahman: Can we match the metric spec naming exactly? Specifically `tokens_per_second_*` (not `toks_per_s`) and `latency_ms_p95` (not `p95_latency_ms`). Also please include `sample_count` so we can compare stability requirements with prod canary windows.
Noah Patel: Updated schema to mirror perf-canary metric field names and added `sample_count`. Also added a schema test that fails if field names change.

Logan Wright: +1 on schema stability. One concern: `region` being "offline" could be confusing when someone tries to join with prod. Could we document that `region=offline` is a sentinel and should be treated separately?
Noah Patel: Added note in docs and a CLI flag `--region` for override when we’re running benchmarks that correspond to a particular fleet/region.

Allison Grant: Please keep the exporter deterministic; otherwise it’ll be noisy in incident diffs. Also for CSV, empty fields should be empty string rather than "null" to play nicer with our existing tools.
Noah Patel: Sorting is now explicit and CSV writer uses empty string for missing optional metadata (kernel_family/runtime_git_sha/quantization_profile).
Marcus Reed: This will be super useful for ENG-2855. Can you also emit `prompt_shape_id` rather than raw prompt file names? The canary matrix uses shape IDs.
Noah Patel: Done; mapping now normalizes to `prompt_shape_id` and logs a warning if it can’t map a run (falls back to `unknown`).
Nadia Rahman: Approved once you add one more test ensuring `streaming` is normalized to "true"/"false" consistently across jsonl and csv.
Noah Patel: Added test; exporter normalizes streaming to boolean in jsonl and lower-case string in CSV.
merge_details: Merged via squash into main by Noah Patel after approvals; no follow-up required. Downstream usage tracked in ENG-2855.
